research_question: Does adding optional head gestures (IMU) to SSVEP selection increase correctly confirmed messages per minute, and for which synthetic patient profiles?
disclaimer: SIMULATED. Synthetic EEG and synthetic head motion decoded by the real FBCCA and gesture code. Not empirical or clinical evidence.

conditions.label: M4: hybrid EEG selection + IMU confirmation (always on)

metrics_definitions.cmpm: correctly confirmed messages per minute of task time
metrics_definitions.mean_task_s: mean time per requested message (latency), incl. failed attempts until timeout
metrics_definitions.accidental_activations_per_hour: false gesture events that changed something (false step YES/NO, spurious tilt-back) per hour
metrics_definitions.corrections_per_message: rejected highlights + Go-back selections + tilt-backs per requested message
metrics_definitions.idle_false_sent_per_hour: messages sent during a no-control block (patient attends nothing)
metrics_definitions.calibration_overhead_s: protocol time for the calibrations the condition needs
metrics_definitions.regret_vs_oracle: oracle CMPM (best fixed candidate policy in hindsight) - condition CMPM

limitations: SIMULATION ONLY. EEG and head motion are synthetic; gesture amplitudes, timings, failure rates and incidental movement are modelling assumptions (acquisition/motion_sim.py), not patient data. Only the stationary IMU noise floor comes from a real (not worn) Unicorn recording.
The simulated patient always intends the right answer; all errors come from the decoders (real FBCCA and real gesture-detector code on synthetic signals, held-out trials).
Gesture outcomes are drawn from a finite held-out pool per profile and replicate; false activations are Poisson at the rate measured on 15 min of held-out synthetic natural movement.
Head-motion EEG artifacts are modelled only for the high_motion profile.
M4 runs hybrid even where the calibration marks gestures unusable (the engine would refuse). It shows what ASSUMING hybrid is better costs; it is not a recommended configuration.
The oracle is chosen in hindsight on the same test sessions; regret against it is a best-case bound, not an achievable target.
Calibration overhead is protocol time only (EEG 2/3/5-target calibrations; gesture protocol), amortised over an assumed 30-minute session.
The policy model (policy.py) is evaluated here against Monte-Carlo simulation of the same simulator; agreement says nothing about real patients.
No clinical validation. No real patient data. Real-EEG / real-IMU capability estimates require the headset.
